scenario: 系统设计面，面试官问「一个 topic 的量太大，单消费者读不过来，你怎么扩？」你想说「开一个 consumer group，分区分给多个消费者并行读」，但一时说不利索。
scenario_en: In a system design round the interviewer asks how you scale reads when one consumer can't keep up with a busy topic. You want to say "put the consumers in a consumer group and split the partitions across them" but blank.
q: 想说「放进一个消费者组，每个分区归一个消费者，并行分担」，哪句最地道？
q_en: You want to say "put them in one consumer group and each partition goes to one consumer" — which line lands?
options: We make a consumer group so the queue split the partitions to every consumer to be parallel and faster.
We put the consumers in one consumer group, and each partition goes to exactly one consumer, so they share the load.
So we, we have like a group of consumers, and the partitions get, you know, kind of spread out so more than one can read at the same time...
Consumers are organized into a consumer group whereby each partition is assigned to precisely one member for parallel consumption.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs Chinglish/打转：「each partition goes to exactly one consumer」一句点出分配机制；「the queue split the partitions」主谓错、像没真用过。
why: 消费者组的机制是「每个分区归组里恰好一个消费者」，一句带出并行分担。主谓错或打转都露怯。
why_en: Put the consumers in one consumer group and each partition goes to exactly one consumer — that names the mechanism, not just the word.
whenOtherWins: 若瓶颈在单分区自己太热，加消费者也没用，得先按 key 重新分区；此时谈 consumer group 是答错方向。
options_en: We make a consumer group so the queue split the partitions to every consumer to be parallel and faster.
We put the consumers in one consumer group, and each partition goes to exactly one consumer, so they share the load.
So we, we have like a group of consumers, and the partitions get, you know, kind of spread out so more than one can read at the same time...
Consumers are organized into a consumer group whereby each partition is assigned to precisely one member for parallel consumption.
optionMeanings: 「the queue split」主谓不搭的中式表达。
点出「每分区归一个消费者」的分配机制。
「like a group of，kind of spread out」一路打转。
optionMeanings_en: "The queue split" — subject-verb mismatch, Chinglish.
Names the assignment: one partition per consumer.
Loops on "like a group, kind of spread out."
Written-register "whereby, precisely one member."
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方听出你在硬拼词，没真用过。
对方立刻懂：怎么并行、怎么分担。
等半天，没听到「一个分区归谁」。
像背文档，不像会怎么部署。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They hear forced keywords, not real experience.
They instantly get how it parallelizes and shares load.
They wait and never hear who owns a partition.
Sounds recited, not like how you'd deploy it.

抓住分区→单消费者→分担的链条。
错在打转，分配关系始终没出口。
错在语域，书面体口语显僵。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: broken collocation, mechanism unclear.
Nails partition to one consumer to shared load.
Wrong: looping, the assignment never lands.
Wrong register — book style feels stiff aloud.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一组一起消费同一个 topic 的消费者；系统把分区分配给组内成员，让它们并行读又不重复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A consumer group is a set of consumers reading the same topic together; the broker splits partitions among them so they read in parallel without overlap.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个 topic 被切成的并行子队列，每个分区内消息有序;分区数决定并行度上限。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A partition is one of the parallel sub-queues a topic is split into; messages are ordered within a partition and the count caps parallelism.

scenario: Nyxa 后端面，面试官问「你的消费者怎么保证不重复处理？」你想说「实际拿到的是 at-least-once，所以让消费者幂等去重，凑出 effectively-once」，但术语卡住了。
scenario_en: In a Nyxa backend round the interviewer asks how your consumer avoids double-processing. You want to say "you actually get at-least-once, so make the consumer idempotent and dedupe for effectively-once" but blank on the terms.
q: 想说「实际是 at-least-once，靠幂等去重凑出 effectively-once」，哪句是工程师的说法？
q_en: You want to say "it's at-least-once, so idempotent dedupe gets you effectively-once" — which line is how an engineer says it?
options: We use exactly-one delivery so the message never come twice and no need to worry the duplicate.
So the delivery is like, it can maybe send twice, so we have to, to handle the same thing coming again somehow, you know...
The system guarantees at-least-once delivery semantics, therefore consumers must implement idempotent processing to tolerate duplicates.
In practice you get at-least-once, so we make the consumer idempotent and dedupe — that buys you effectively-once.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 造词/打转：「at-least-once + idempotent dedupe = effectively-once」一句点出机制；「exactly-one」是造错的词形，露怯。
why: 真实系统多是 at-least-once，靠幂等去重凑 effectively-once。词形写成 exactly-one 或打转都露怯。
why_en: In practice it's at-least-once, so an idempotent consumer that dedupes gets you effectively-once — that's the real chain.
whenOtherWins: 若平台原生支持事务性 exactly-once 且你确实开了，就直说 we rely on exactly-once semantics，不必再讲手动去重。
options_en: We use exactly-one delivery so the message never come twice and no need to worry the duplicate.
So the delivery is like, it can maybe send twice, so we have to, to handle the same thing coming again somehow, you know...
The system guarantees at-least-once delivery semantics, therefore consumers must implement idempotent processing to tolerate duplicates.
In practice you get at-least-once, so we make the consumer idempotent and dedupe — that buys you effectively-once.
optionMeanings: at-least-once 打底,去重凑成只生效一次。
optionMeanings_en: "Exactly-one" — wrong term form, plus bad grammar.
Loops on "maybe send twice, somehow."
Book register: "guarantees…semantics, therefore."
At-least-once plus idempotent dedupe = effectively-once.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方听出你没真用过投递语义。
等半天，没听到怎么处理重复。
像背定义,不像会怎么落地。
对方立刻懂:靠去重顶住重复。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They hear you've never used delivery semantics.
They wait and never hear how duplicates are handled.
Sounds like a recited definition, not a build.
They instantly get it: dedupe absorbs the duplicates.
optionDirectness: 错在词形，exactly-once 才对。
错在打转,去重方案没出口。
错在语域,念稿体显生硬。
抓住投递语义→幂等→凑出一次效果。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong form; the term is exactly-once.
Wrong: looping, the dedupe plan never lands.
Wrong register — recital feels stiff aloud.
Nails semantics to idempotence to effective-once.

termDefinitions.meaning: 投递语义：消息保证至少送到一次，但可能重复，所以消费者要能容忍重复。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: At-least-once is a delivery guarantee where a message arrives at least once but may be duplicated, so the consumer must tolerate repeats.

termDefinitions.meaning: 投递语义:每条消息的效果恰好生效一次;端到端实现代价高,常靠幂等去重来近似。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Exactly-once means each message takes effect precisely once; true end-to-end it is costly, so people approximate it with idempotent dedupe.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一条消息处理一次和处理多次结果相同,所以重放重复不会造成额外影响。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means processing the same message once or many times gives the same result, so a replayed duplicate has no extra effect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 去重:靠消息唯一 id 或 key 记住处理过的,再来同一条就跳过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dedupe means dropping repeats by remembering a message's unique id or key and skipping it if seen again.

termDefinitions.meaning: 投递上是 at-least-once,但靠去重让业务效果看起来只发生一次。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Effectively-once is at-least-once delivery made to have a once-only business effect by deduplicating.

scenario: 面试官追问「有些消息一直处理失败、卡住后面，你怎么办？」你想说「重试几次后甩进死信队列，别堵住后面的」，但 dead-letter queue 一时说不出口。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks what you do when some messages keep failing and block the rest. You want to say "after a few retries, route them to a dead-letter queue so they don't block the line" but blank on the term.
q: 想说「重试几次后甩进死信队列，一条坏消息别堵住后面」，哪句最地道？
q_en: You want to say "after a few retries, send it to a dead-letter queue so one bad message doesn't block the rest" — which line lands?
options: After a few retries we route it to a dead-letter queue, so one bad message doesn't block the rest.
We put the fail message to a dead letter box so it will not stop other message to be handle.
So if a message keeps, keeps failing, we kind of move it somewhere else so it, so it doesn't, you know, hold up everything behind it...
Messages that repeatedly fail processing are relegated to a dead-letter queue for subsequent manual inspection and remediation.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs Chinglish/念稿：「route it to a dead-letter queue after a few retries」一句点出机制;「dead letter box」是错词形,露怯。
why: 机制是「重试 N 次后 route 到 dead-letter queue」，一句带出不堵主线。词形写成 dead letter box 就露怯。
why_en: After a few retries we route it to a dead-letter queue so one bad message doesn't block the rest — that names the mechanism.
whenOtherWins: 若失败是全局暂时故障(下游全挂),别急着进死信,该整体退避重试;死信是给「个别一直失败」的消息。
options_en: After a few retries we route it to a dead-letter queue, so one bad message doesn't block the rest.
We put the fail message to a dead letter box so it will not stop other message to be handle.
So if a message keeps, keeps failing, we kind of move it somewhere else so it, so it doesn't, you know, hold up everything behind it...
Messages that repeatedly fail processing are relegated to a dead-letter queue for subsequent manual inspection and remediation.
optionMeanings: 重试后 route 到死信队列,不堵主线。
optionMeanings_en: Route to a DLQ after retries, line stays unblocked.
Wrong forms: "dead letter box, fail message."
Loops on "keeps keeps, move somewhere else."
Book style: "relegated to…for subsequent."
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方立刻懂:坏消息被隔离,不阻塞。
对方听出你没真配过死信。
等半天,没听到「死信队列」四个字。
像背运维手册,不像会怎么处置。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They instantly get it: bad message isolated, no block.
They hear you've never wired up a DLQ.
They wait and never hear the words dead-letter queue.
Sounds like a recited runbook, not a real call.
optionDirectness: 抓住重试→死信→不堵后面的链条。
错在词形,DLQ 才是对的写法。
错在打转,隔离机制没出口。
错在语域,书面体口语显僵。
optionDirectness_en: Nails retries to DLQ to unblocked line.
Wrong form; it's a dead-letter queue.
Wrong: looping, the isolation never lands.
Wrong register — book style stiff aloud.

termDefinitions.meaning: 专门收「重试多次仍失败」消息的旁路队列;把坏消息挪出主线,方便事后排查,不再阻塞后面的消息。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A dead-letter queue is a side queue for messages that keep failing after retries; it moves bad messages off the main line for later inspection so they stop blocking others.

termDefinitions.meaning: 处理失败后再试一次;通常配退避和上限,超过次数才转入死信。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A retry re-attempts a failed message, usually with backoff and a cap, after which it is routed to the dead-letter queue.

scenario: Corvid 系统设计面，面试官问「同一个用户的事件必须按顺序处理，你怎么保证？」你想说「用 user id 当 partition key，同一 key 落同一分区，天然有序」，但表达打了结。
scenario_en: In a Corvid design round the interviewer asks how you keep one user's events in order. You want to say "use the user id as the partition key, so the same key lands on the same partition and stays ordered" but tangle up.
q: 想说「用 user id 做 partition key，同一 key 落同一分区、天然有序」，哪句最地道？
q_en: You want to say "key by user id, so the same key lands on the same partition, in order" — which line lands?
options: So to keep the order we, we send the same kind of events to, to the same place so they don't get, get mixed up in the wrong order...
We set a partition key so the same key always go to same partition and keep the order right.
We key by user id, so all of one user's events hit the same partition and stay in order.
By designating the partition key, records sharing a key are routed to an identical partition, thereby preserving their relative ordering.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs 打转/念稿：「key by user id → same partition → in order」一句点出因果;泛泛「the same place」没说清 key 决定路由。
why: 顺序保证的机制是「同一 partition key 路由到同一分区，分区内有序」。用 user id 当 key 一句带出。
why_en: Key by user id so all of one user's events hit the same partition and stay in order — that names why ordering holds.
whenOtherWins: 若要的是全局有序(跨所有用户),单靠 key 不够,得单分区或加序列号;此时谈 partition key 只保住了分区内有序。
options_en: So to keep the order we, we send the same kind of events to, to the same place so they don't get, get mixed up in the wrong order...
We set a partition key so the same key always go to same partition and keep the order right.
We key by user id, so all of one user's events hit the same partition and stay in order.
By designating the partition key, records sharing a key are routed to an identical partition, thereby preserving their relative ordering.

「always go to，the order right」搭配偏中式。
key by user id→同分区→有序,因果清楚。

错在语域,书面体口语显僵。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong: vague looping, key-routes-record unsaid.
Weak collocation; the key-to-partition cause is soft.
Nails key to same partition to in-order.

termDefinitions.meaning: 决定一条消息落到哪个分区的字段;同一个 key 的消息总路由到同一分区,从而保住彼此的顺序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The partition key is the field that decides which partition a message lands on; the same key always routes to the same partition, preserving order among those messages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消息处理的先后顺序;多数队列只保证「同一分区内」有序,跨分区不保证。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Ordering is the sequence in which messages are processed; most queues guarantee it only within a single partition, not across partitions.

scenario: 实时数仓面试，面试官问「每分钟统计一次点击数，晚到的事件怎么处理？」你想说「开一分钟 tumbling window，用 watermark 决定何时关窗、丢太晚的」，但术语卡壳。
scenario_en: In a real-time analytics interview, they ask how you count clicks per minute and handle late events. You want to say "a one-minute tumbling window, and a watermark decides when to close it and drop late events" but blank.
q: 想说「一分钟 tumbling window，watermark 决定何时关窗、丢太晚的事件」，哪句是工程师的说法？
q_en: You want to say "a one-minute tumbling window, and a watermark decides when to close it and drop late events" — which line lands?
options: We use a rolling window and a water line to know when the late data is too late to count.
We run a one-minute tumbling window, and a watermark tells us when to close it and drop late events.
So we kind of group the events into, into time chunks, and then we have a thing that decides when it's, when it's too late for the old ones...
A tumbling window aggregates events over fixed intervals, while a watermark demarcates the threshold beyond which late arrivals are discarded.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 造词/打转：「tumbling window + watermark tells us when to close」点出机制;「rolling window，water line」是造错的词形。
why: 机制是「tumbling window 分桶，watermark 决定关窗和丢晚到」。造词 water line 或打转都露怯。
why_en: A one-minute tumbling window and a watermark that tells us when to close it and drop late events — that's the exact vocabulary.
whenOtherWins: 若要连续滑动统计而非不重叠分桶,就说 sliding window;若必须收晚到数据,配 allowed lateness 而不是直接丢。
options_en: We use a rolling window and a water line to know when the late data is too late to count.
We run a one-minute tumbling window, and a watermark tells us when to close it and drop late events.
So we kind of group the events into, into time chunks, and then we have a thing that decides when it's, when it's too late for the old ones...
A tumbling window aggregates events over fixed intervals, while a watermark demarcates the threshold beyond which late arrivals are discarded.
optionMeanings: 定长分桶 + 到点关窗,机制到位。
optionMeanings_en: Invented forms: "rolling window, water line."
Tumbling window + watermark closing — mechanism lands.
Loops on "time chunks, a thing that," never names it.
Book style: "aggregates…demarcates the threshold."
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方听出你只听过没真跑过。
对方立刻懂:怎么分桶、怎么处理晚到。
等半天,没听到 window 和 watermark。
像背文档,不像会怎么配作业。
optionScenarioImpacts_en: They hear heard-not-run vocabulary.
They instantly get bucketing and late handling.

抓住分桶→watermark 关窗→丢晚到。
错在打转,两个术语都没出口。
错在语域,书面体口语显僵。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong forms; it's tumbling window and watermark.
Nails bucketing to watermark-close to drop-late.
Wrong: looping, neither term lands.
Wrong register — book style stiff aloud.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把流按固定时长切成不重叠的桶(如每 1 分钟一个),每条事件只属于一个桶,用来做周期聚合。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A tumbling window slices a stream into fixed, non-overlapping buckets (e.g. one per minute); each event belongs to exactly one, used for periodic aggregation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按固定长度但连续滑动的窗口,窗口之间会重叠,同一事件可落入多个窗口。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A sliding window is a fixed-length window that advances continuously and overlaps, so one event can fall into several windows.

termDefinitions.meaning: 流处理里表示「事件时间已推进到某点」的标记;它决定何时认为窗口收齐、可以关窗,晚于它的事件算迟到。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A watermark marks how far event-time has advanced in a stream; it decides when a window is considered complete and can close, and events after it count as late.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对持续到来的事件流实时计算(而非攒成批离线跑),常配窗口和 watermark。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stream processing computes over a continuous flow of events in real time rather than in offline batches, typically using windows and watermarks.

scenario: 面试官问「上线后发现处理逻辑有 bug，历史消息要重新跑一遍，你怎么做？」你想说「把 offset 倒回早一点、从那儿 replay 重放」，但一时说不利索。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks how you reprocess history after shipping a bug in the handler. You want to say "rewind the offset and replay from an earlier point" but blank on the phrasing.
q: 想说「把消费 offset 倒回，从早一点的位置 replay 重放」，哪句最地道？
q_en: You want to say "rewind the offset and replay from an earlier point to reprocess" — which line lands?
options: We roll back the read point and read again from before to redo the messages.
So if we need to redo it, we can kind of go back to, to an earlier spot and, and read all of it over again from there...
To reprocess historical data, the consumer offset is reset to a prior position and the event log is replayed.
We rewind the offset and replay from an earlier point to reprocess.
tradeoff: 地道口语 vs Chinglish/念稿：「rewind the offset and replay」一句点出机制;「read point，read again」是错词形,露怯。
why: 重放机制是「reset/rewind offset，从早一点 replay」。写成 read point 或打转都不地道。
why_en: We rewind the offset and replay from an earlier point to reprocess — that's the exact phrasing engineers use.
whenOtherWins: 若日志已过保留期、早期消息被清了,就 replay 不回去,得从备份或数仓回灌;此时谈 offset 重放已不适用。
options_en: We roll back the read point and read again from before to redo the messages.
So if we need to redo it, we can kind of go back to, to an earlier spot and, and read all of it over again from there...
To reprocess historical data, the consumer offset is reset to a prior position and the event log is replayed.
We rewind the offset and replay from an earlier point to reprocess.
optionMeanings: 「kind of go back，an earlier spot」打转。
「is reset to a prior position」被动念稿腔。
rewind offset + replay,机制一句到位。
optionMeanings_en: Wrong forms: "read point, read again from before."
Loops on "kind of go back, an earlier spot."
Passive book style: "is reset to a prior position."
Rewind offset + replay — mechanism in one line.
optionScenarioImpacts: 对方听出你没真做过重放。
等半天,没听到 offset 和 replay。
像念文档,不像会怎么操作。
对方立刻懂:从哪儿重放、怎么倒回。

They wait and never hear offset or replay.
Sounds read aloud, not like a real operation.

错在打转,重放位置没出口。
错在语域,被动书面体显僵。
抓住 rewind offset→replay→重跑历史。
optionDirectness_en: Wrong forms; it's offset and replay.
Wrong: looping, the replay point never lands.
Wrong register — passive book style stiff.
Nails rewind-offset to replay to reprocess.

termDefinitions.meaning: 消费者在分区里读到的位置游标;把它调回早一点,就能从那个位置重新读。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An offset is the cursor marking how far a consumer has read in a partition; move it back and you re-read from that point.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 offset 倒回后从旧位置重新消费一遍消息,用来在改了逻辑或修了 bug 后重算历史。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replay/reprocess means rewinding the offset and consuming messages again from an earlier point to recompute history after a logic change or bug fix.

scenario: 面试官问「既然是 at-least-once，重复消息会不会把余额扣两次？」你想说「消费者是幂等的，按 message id 去重，重放重复是 no-op」，但术语一时说不顺。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: since it's at-least-once, won't a duplicate charge twice? You want to say "the consumer is idempotent — we dedupe on message id, so a duplicate is a no-op" but blank.
q: 想说「消费者幂等，按 message id 去重，重放重复是 no-op」，哪句是工程师的说法？
q_en: You want to say "the consumer is idempotent — dedupe on message id, so a duplicate is a no-op" — which line lands?
options: The consumer is idempotent — we dedupe on the message id, so reprocessing a duplicate is a no-op.
The consumer is idempotence, so if the same message come again it will not do the thing two times.
So the consumer, it kind of, if it sees the same one again it just, you know, doesn't do anything, so it's safe to, to run it twice...
An idempotent consumer deduplicates on a unique message identifier such that reprocessing a duplicate event yields no additional effect.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs 错词形/打转：「idempotent，dedupe on the message id，a no-op」一句点出机制;「is idempotence」是词形错。
why: 幂等消费者的机制是「按 message id 去重，重复处理是 no-op」。词形写成 idempotence 或打转都露怯。
why_en: The consumer is idempotent — we dedupe on the message id, so reprocessing a duplicate is a no-op — that names the mechanism.
whenOtherWins: 若操作天然幂等(如覆盖写、set 到定值),就不必额外去重,直说 the write is naturally idempotent;去重表是给非幂等操作兜底。

The consumer is idempotence, so if the same message come again it will not do the thing two times.
So the consumer, it kind of, if it sees the same one again it just, you know, doesn't do anything, so it's safe to, to run it twice...
An idempotent consumer deduplicates on a unique message identifier such that reprocessing a duplicate event yields no additional effect.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同一条消息处理一次和多次结果相同;幂等消费者对重复消息不会产生额外副作用。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Idempotent means processing a message once or many times yields the same result; an idempotent consumer has no extra side effect on duplicates.

termDefinitions.meaning: 去重:用 message id 或业务 key 记住处理过的消息,再见到同一条就跳过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Dedupe means using a message id or business key to remember handled messages and skip a repeat.

termDefinitions.meaning: no-operation:什么也不做、无副作用的操作;重放重复消息命中去重后就是个 no-op。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A no-op is an operation that does nothing and has no side effect; a deduplicated duplicate ends up as a no-op.

termDefinitions.meaning: 每条消息的唯一标识;去重就以它为键判断是否处理过。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A message id is a unique identifier per message, used as the key to decide whether it was already processed.

scenario: 面试官问「每来一条事件就写一次库，下游扛不住，怎么优化？」你想说「micro-batch，攒几百条 buffer 起来一次性 flush，降低写放大」，但术语卡住了。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks how you optimize when writing to the DB per event overwhelms it. You want to say "micro-batch — buffer a few hundred and flush in one write to cut write amplification" but blank.
q: 想说「micro-batch，攒几百条 buffer 再一次 flush，降低写放大」，哪句最地道？
q_en: You want to say "micro-batch — buffer a few hundred events and flush in one write" — which line lands?
options: So instead of writing every single one, we kind of collect a bunch first and then, then write them all together to save, you know, the writes...
We do a small batch, buffer some message then write one time, to reduce the write pressure.
We micro-batch — buffer a few hundred events and flush in one write — to cut write amplification.
Micro-batching accumulates a small quantity of records and commits them as a single write to reduce write amplification.
tradeoff: 地道术语 vs Chinglish/打转：「micro-batch，buffer then flush in one write」点出机制;「write one time，write pressure」是中式搭配。
why: 机制是「buffer 攒几百条，一次 flush 写库」，降低写放大。写成 write one time 或打转都露怯。
why_en: We micro-batch — buffer a few hundred events and flush in one write — to cut write amplification; that names the mechanism.
whenOtherWins: 若延迟要求极严(近实时逐条),攒批会加延迟,就别 micro-batch,逐条写或缩小批量;攒批是拿延迟换吞吐。

Micro-batching accumulates a small quantity of records and commits them as a single write to reduce write amplification.

termDefinitions.meaning: 不逐条处理,而是攒一小批(几百条)再一次性写出;拿一点延迟换更高吞吐、更少写次数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Micro-batching buffers a small batch of records (a few hundred) and writes them at once, trading a little latency for higher throughput and fewer writes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把 buffer 里攒的数据一次性真正写到下游(库/磁盘)的动作。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A flush is the act of actually writing the buffered data out to the downstream store or disk in one go.

termDefinitions.meaning: 写放大:一份逻辑数据引发的实际写操作次数;逐条写会放大写次数,攒批能显著降低。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Write amplification is how many actual writes one logical piece of data triggers; per-event writes amplify it, and batching reduces it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 临时暂存区,先把事件攒在这里,到量或到时间再一起 flush。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A buffer is a temporary holding area where events accumulate until a size or time threshold triggers a flush.
